source_text: Bona igitur concupiscentia naturalis (erubescis enim dicere carnalis) quae cum intra modum suum tenetur nulla mali aspersione turpatur
pass_a_gloss: Goods therefore desire natural ( erubescis for to-say carnal ) which when/with within modum his-own holds no of-evil aspersione turpatur.

lemmas.lexica: LS naturalis; Blaise malum naturale=evil as a nature
LS concupiscentia=eager desire; Blaise Christian usage often sexual desire vs nuptiae
LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis

pass_b_english: Natural desire is therefore good. When kept within its proper measure, it is stained by no taint of evil.

choices.why: Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.
Julian distinguishes nuptiae from concupiscentia; do not flatten to 'lust' as a nature-sin substance.
Keep Julian's good-of-nature vs good-of-will contrast; do not baptize as 'grace'.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
